title: Strings - single vs double quotes and concatenation
keywords: how to interpolate variables in a string
answer: Single-quoted strings print text exactly as written. Double-quoted strings replace $variables and interpret escape sequences like \n. Join strings with the dot operator, never with +.
pitfall: Using + to join strings adds numbers instead. '5' + '5' is 10, while '5' . '5' is '55'.

title: Comparing strings - strcmp, case-insensitive compare, == vs ===
answer: Use === when two strings must be exactly equal, including case. Use strcasecmp for a case-insensitive comparison. strcmp returns 0 when strings are equal, a negative number when the first is smaller, and a positive number otherwise.
pitfall: strcmp returns 0 for equal strings, and 0 is falsy in PHP. Never use it directly in an if condition without comparing to 0.

title: Formatting strings - sprintf, number_format, escaping output
answer: sprintf builds a string from a template with placeholders like %s for strings and %d for integers. number_format formats money and large numbers with commas and decimals. Always escape user text with htmlspecialchars before printing it into HTML.
output: Hello Prabh, your total is Rs 1234567.891,234,567.89<b>Hi</b>
pitfall: Printing user input directly into HTML without htmlspecialchars lets an attacker inject scripts. Escape on output, every time.

title: String functions - length, case, replace, trim, split
answer: strlen counts bytes, trim removes whitespace from both ends, str_replace swaps text, explode splits a string into an array and implode joins an array back into a string. substr returns part of a string.
pitfall: strlen counts bytes, not characters. For Hindi or emoji text it returns a larger number than the visible character count.

title: String interpolation and heredoc
answer: Wrap a variable in curly braces inside a double-quoted string when it touches other text. For long multi-line text, heredoc keeps the text readable without escaping quotes.
output:
Hello, Prabh Singh!Dear Prabh,
Your order is ready.
Thank you!
pitfall: Heredoc closing label must start at the very beginning of its line, with no spaces before it, or PHP reports a parse error.

title: Unicode text - why strlen can mislead and what to use instead
answer: PHP strings are byte sequences. strlen counts bytes, so accented text and emoji count as more than one per visible character. For character-accurate work, use the mbstring functions mb_strlen and mb_substr, and save files as UTF-8. This example is syntax-checked only because mbstring is an optional extension and may not be installed.
pitfall: Cutting a UTF-8 string with substr can split a character in half and produce broken output. Use mb_substr for user-facing text.

title: Searching inside strings - strpos, str_contains, starts/ends with
keywords: how to check if a string contains text
answer: Use str_contains to check if one string is inside another. Use strpos only when you also need the position, and compare its result with === false, because position 0 means found at the start. str_starts_with and str_ends_with check the beginning and end.
pitfall: strpos returns 0 when the text is found at position 0, and 0 is falsy. Never write if (strpos(...)) without comparing to false with ===.
